body:
Pelegia, also recorded as Pin, Pell and Pelagia, is one player character.

Meeting the company as Pin

Pin is a player character. In his introduction to the company, he gives his name and stays close to Carmen while meeting unfamiliar companions. The scene places him among the adventurers without establishing a home island.

Care after the fight

In a later encounter he offers healing and acknowledges Carmen’s final shot. This preserves an act of practical support without inventing a complete biography, allegiance or later fate.

A Seeker and civic servant

Pelegia explores the contaminated harpy cave with the Seekers. Despite feeling afraid, Pelegia insists that the corrupted corpse deserves burial while the company investigates. Vessalia offers emotional shelter while Di’Trillio, Minerva and Fenwick give the investigation a shared structure.

Later service includes gathering Mama Tabitha’s ingredients, preparing Papirak’s grave, planning a mausoleum and helping with fundraising. These trusted tasks give Pelegia purpose within Pristinia.

A leader has to be worth following

At the New Vanguard’s tests, Pin defines leadership through being worthy of followers and aligning them toward a common goal. He gives honor the language of integrity and wisdom the language of applied knowledge. He eventually names Severina as his preferred leader.

His answers to the battlefield problems are harder than a simple promise to save everyone. He chooses the battalion and relic in one imagined situation and speaks of recovering the friend afterward. Elsewhere he accepts a fallen companion’s sacrifice rather than making a stranger pay for it. These are hypothetical answers in a test, not killings he carried out or proof that he would never change his mind.

People before the things meant to help them

When Thorn is lost, Pelegia offers help and questions the expense of obtaining magical equipment before retrieving a fallen teammate. He has already spent money on gifts and pledged resources toward the company’s obligations. He favors a workable shared font over a purchase that could place the team deeper in debt.

His disagreement with the price of help does not become a refusal to pay for Thorn. He agrees to speak with Ryvyt and offers his own gold for what is still needed. He gives the company its clearest statement of purpose: people are loved, items are used. The possible value of an item to the Veilguard is a bonus beside bringing their friend home.

Ryvyt can craft, but materials are scarce. Their conversation begins work on a solution; it does not establish a completed item, a settled bill or a resurrection performed by Pelegia. His principle becomes concrete through bargaining, contribution and the willingness to make a promise expensive.

The Larkhollow expeditions

Recorded as Pelagia, Pelegia urges retreat from Hana’s tower when the company is in danger, then returns with Ryvyt to question market residents about the forest. Their differing apparent travel durations remain unexplained.

Pin and the river’s call

Recorded as Pin, Pelegia joins Fenwick, Ryvyt and Minerva in the search for Selwyn. The Eternal River draws him toward it against his will. Ryvyt holds and pulls him back, yet his body visibly ages seven years. The narrator also records an unusual sense of health and happiness; that sensation does not show the effect is harmless or reversible.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Bargaining for the people who must come home

Pin tries to negotiate for Selwyn’s body while fighting the shadowy figures, rejecting a demand for his actual arm. He continues seeking a way to take both Selwyn and Minerva back without more killing. When Minerva chooses to remain, he accepts her lock of hair and promises to seek a healer if she does not return.

The roots are released from Selwyn, but a branch remains. No completed journey home, resurrection or restoration of either companion is shown in this scene.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Standing beside Ryvyt at Hana’s tower

Pin accompanied Ryvyt, Saelihn, Oya and Fenwick on the return to Hana’s tower. When the Children of Viota threatened Minerva, Pin recalled that she had been promised a way back. Inside, Hana held Pin and Oya with telekinesis until Saelihn warped them free. Pin later used a shadow attack against a clockwork opponent.

When Hana lay dead and Ryvyt wanted a burial, Pin offered to help. They first continued the investigation together. In the basement, they examined the broken Tik, missing parts and damaged writing; above, Pin suggested that perfect illusions might preserve the paintings. The suggestion was not yet a completed work. Familiar-looking seasonal figures also did not establish a recognized identity: the narrator described their features as common.

The record reaches a roofless upper floor and the painting titled The Gardener Beneath the Moon, then stops. Pin’s part in this expedition is established by the scene’s explicit names and narrator references. Read the full tower account →

Shared histories

Read the Seekers’ complete history →

Read Pin’s dark-expanse expedition →

Recorded scenes

  • Pin introduces himself
  • An offer of healing
  • Acknowledging Carmen’s shot

Helping can mean leaving the sea

Pell looks for useful plants near the Remote Fishing Village, hoping to earn something when supplies seem scarce. He joins Thorn’s approach to a sea serpent despite his fear of deep water. Before they go, he gives clear permission for her to carry him away if necessary.

That is the help he eventually needs. Toadimus turns back, Thorn takes wing, and Pell is carried out. A sudden storm hides the village as they return, sending the journey onward toward the observatory. The encounter does not show a tamed creature or a sea battle; it shows a frightened companion trusting someone else to get him away.

An invitation accepted cautiously

Pin accepts a mask at the Eversong and lets his shadow companion watch the gathering. The narrator makes clear that the guests saw it move. When the company’s shadows become hostile, his precaution is caught inside the same danger.

He keeps working through impaired sight, proposes surrender to the leading foe and later asks after the others’ worlds. The full encounter preserves his willingness to speak beside the violence, without granting the enemy a departure the ending does not show.

brief.status: Continues exploring Hana’s tower with Ryvyt after her death; the investigation and intended burial remain unfinished.
brief.basis: Existing public dossier, explicit status facts and named timeline participants. Selected events are a reading guide, not a complete list or a ranking of importance.

profile.personality: Pell is frightened in ways the record never mocks and practical in ways fear does not erase. The most important part of Pell’s cave history is moral clarity: a corrupted corpse is still somebody’s child, and danger does not cancel the obligation to recognize a life that existed before the horror. Introduces himself to unfamiliar companions while remaining close to Carmen.
profile.achievements: Pell helps the Seekers explore a cave marked by contamination, crystalline anomalies, malformed harpies, and a dead body whose condition becomes evidence. Staying present long enough to observe, argue for burial, and continue with the company is an achievement of endurance rather than spectacle. Pell gives the unnamed cave dead a last prayer before the collapse. At Papirak’s funeral he describes service as a source of purpose after doubting his usefulness on expeditions. The September ingredient quest also shows him helping examine Bogdan, then receiving treatment for an accidental anaesthetic exposure. The tower expedition shows her choosing retreat when the company is in danger. On the market journey, she and Ryvyt experience different apparent travel durations; no single mechanism is established. Offers healing after a fight and acknowledges Carmen’s final shot. Tries to negotiate Selwyn’s release and accepts Minerva’s lock of hair as an obligation to seek help.
profile.relationships: Vessalia’s attention gives Pell emotional shelter, while Di’Trillio’s technical observations and Minerva and Fenwick’s investigation give the fear a shared structure. Pell’s insistence on burial also changes the group’s relationship with the dead: the body cannot be treated only as a clue, obstacle, or contaminated object. Recorded alongside Carmen and the adventuring company; further relationships are not established here.
